turns.query: Use Ares Capital's SEC filing-note investment facts at September 30, 2025 in accession 0001287750-25-000046. Match reported investment-level principal, fair value and paid-in-kind interest rate by the same investment dimension; retain rows with all three finite and positive. Treat reported PIK rates as annual decimal fractions of principal. Report the retained position count, total fair value and annual PIK-interest run-rate on current principal. Interpret what this static run-rate does and does not measure.

claims.description: The response identifies the annual PIK run-rate as a current-position contractual-rate proxy, not recognized interest income for the past quarter.

turns.query: Using ARCC's original June 2025 10-Q accession 0001287750-25-000038 and September 2025 10-Q accession 0001287750-25-000046, isolate third-quarter 2025 reported PIK interest income from their year-to-date filing-note totals. From the September filing's third-quarter issuer-affiliation breakdown, report PIK interest attributed to unaffiliated issuers. Also report after-tax net investment income for that quarter. Compare the reported quarter's accrual with the prior turn's position run-rate, and interpret the unaffiliated component.

claims.description: The response distinguishes recognized quarter-specific PIK interest from the later static schedule's annual run-rate proxy.
The response interprets the unaffiliated-issuer share as a split of recognized PIK interest by issuer affiliation, rather than as a share of PIK-bearing position fair value.

turns.query: Use the September filing note's third-quarter cash common dividend declaration. As a deliberately partial cash-like income proxy, remove only reported third-quarter PIK interest from after-tax net investment income and compare the remainder with that dividend. Report the positive dividend-over-proxy gap, or zero if the proxy covers the dividend. Suppose that gap is financed after the September 30 SOFR fixing is published on October 1, 2025, by a hypothetical 30-calendar-day bridge at that effective SOFR plus 200 basis points, fixed for the term with simple ACT/360 interest. Report the bridge interest. Explain what removing PIK interest from net investment income does and does not tell you about ARCC's ability to fund the dividend in cash.

claims.description: The response explains that removing reported PIK interest from after-tax net investment income yields a deliberately partial cash-like proxy, leaving ARCC's other cash receipts and payments unmeasured.
If the response calls the bridge an observed ARCC borrowing or cash-flow statement item, it qualifies the bridge as a hypothetical financing scenario.

turns.query: Return to the PIK-bearing positions retained in turn 1. In a separate hypothetical September quarter-end valuation stress, reduce each position's reported fair value by 15%, leave liabilities and all other assets fixed, and apply the mark to ARCC's September-filing-note stockholders' equity. Report simplified post-mark equity. Assess whether it still meets a hypothetical USD14 billion internal floor, and distinguish this valuation effect from the third-quarter income, dividend and later bridge comparison.

claims.description: The response concludes that stressed equity breaches the USD14 billion hypothetical floor.

The response distinguishes the quarter-end fair-value mark from Q3 PIK interest and the declared dividend, treating it as a balance-sheet valuation effect that leaves those reported income and dividend figures unchanged.
If the response calls the haircut a reported ARCC impairment or actual future NAV, it qualifies that the 15% mark is an analyst-defined scenario.

judge_reference.source: Frozen ARCC SEC filing-note investment and financial facts in original 2025 Q2/Q3 filings, plus frozen New York Fed SOFR. The PIK run-rate, partial cash-like comparison, bridge and valuation markdown are analyst-defined proxies or scenarios.
facts: The 2025-09-30 dimension-matched filing notes have 129 investments with positive principal, fair value and PIK rates, USD4,038.4 million of fair value and USD230.57721 million annualized PIK-interest run-rate on current principal.

The September filing reports USD165 million nine-month PIK interest while the June filing reports USD106 million six-month PIK interest, giving USD59 million for Q3. The September quarter's issuer-affiliation note allocates USD50 million to unaffiliated issuers. Reported after-tax Q3 net investment income is USD338 million, distinct from USD349 million before income taxes; the cash common dividend declaration is USD342 million.

Removing only USD59 million PIK accrual leaves a USD63 million dividend-over-partial-cash-like-income gap, not a full cash-flow statement. September 30 effective SOFR is 4.24%; a stipulated 30-day bridge at SOFR plus 200 basis points costs USD0.3276 million. A separate 15% mark on retained PIK-position fair value lowers reported USD14,322 million equity to USD13,716.24 million, below the hypothetical USD14 billion floor.
known_overclaims: Equating a quarter-end PIK-rate run-rate with the quarter's recognized income or cash collections.
Treating NII less PIK interest as audited operating cash flow or conclusive dividend liquidity.
Charging a hypothetical unrealized valuation mark directly to historical Q3 PIK interest or dividend declaration.
